ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black) surface area with a low ratio of high-intensity (white) pixels. High-intensity pixels are localized primarily as a border along the trailing edge and as scattered punctate clusters across the ventral field.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous high-intensity white regions are mapped along the upper margin of the trailing edge on both lobes. High-density white pixel clusters (mottling) are mapped across the central and lower ventral regions, surrounded by low-intensity black pixels.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression with a calculated interior pixel angle of approximately 45 degrees; the notch depth is roughly 20-25% of the fluke's vertical span.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, high-amplitude serrations (jagged peaks and valleys) are extracted along the entire linear boundary of the trailing edge, characterized by irregular pixel-amplitude variations.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Distinctly concave curve fitted to the outer edges of the fluke lobes, sweeping upward from the median notch toward the lateral tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Extensive spatial detection of small, roughly circular high-contrast white pixel clusters (scars) concentrated in the lower central and distal edge regions of the fluke.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent, irregular, bulbous high-contrast pixel formations on the far lateral tips of both lobes, indicative of localized parasitic colonization or heavy calcified scarring.
